title: wg: is GroupInfoCode's reserved(0)/success(1) deliberate? (issue, not a PR)
description:
Found while writing draft-atwood-mimi-catchup's response code enum
(2026-11-26). Held: do not send without Mark's OK.

## The observation

Every response code enum in protocol-07 except one puts success at 0:

  KeyMaterialUserCode    success(0), partialSuccess(1), ...
  KeyMaterialClientCode  success(0), keyMaterialExhausted(1), ...
  UpdateResponseCode     success(0), wrongEpoch(1), notAllowed(2), ...
  SubmitResponseCode     accepted(0), notAllowed(1), epochTooOld(2)
  IdentifierQueryCode    success(0), notFound(1), ambiguous(2), ...
  GroupInfoCode          reserved(0), success(1), notAuthorized(2),
                         noSuchRoom(3)

GroupInfoCode is the only one that reserves 0, and it sits in the
document among REPRESENTATION enums that legitimately reserve 0
(GroupInfoRepresentation: reserved(0), full(1), partial(2)), which is a
plausible origin for it.

## Why this is an issue and not a PR

Changing it would change the wire. A response of 0 means success to
five endpoints and "reserved" to one; an implementation that normalized
it would be non-conforming against anything that did not. So it is a
question for the WG, phrased as a question:

  Is GroupInfoCode's reserved(0) with success(1) deliberate? Every
  other response code enum in the document uses 0 for success, and
  GroupInfoCode sits beside representation enums that reserve 0, so it
  reads as though it may have picked the convention up from its
  neighbours. If it is deliberate, a sentence saying so would help; if
  not, it is cheaper to change now than after there are deployments.

## What was NOT worth raising, having looked properly

An earlier reading of this had two further findings. Both dissolved on
checking, and they are recorded so they are not raised again:

1. "Several enums declare both reserved(0) and success(0)." FALSE. That
   was an artifact of an awk range expression merging adjacent enums.
   No enum does this.

2. "Three names for one concept: notAllowed, notAuthorized, forbidden."
   WEAK. The prose gives each a different scope:
   - notAllowed: policy OR authorization prevented accepting a write
     (UpdateResponseCode, SubmitResponseCode)
   - notAuthorized: the requester was not authorized to read a
     GroupInfo (GroupInfoCode)
   - forbidden: use of the ENDPOINT is not allowed, or an unspecified
     field or combination of fields is not allowed (IdentifierQueryCode)
   Three scopes, not three synonyms. Normalizing them would lose
   meaning, so no PR.

The one editorial inconsistency that did survive is SubmitResponseCode's
accepted(0) where the other four say success(0), with word-for-word
identical prose. That is prepared as a PR on branch
submit-response-success in ~/PROJECT/IETF-wg/mimi-protocol, commit
fd140d3, based on upstream/main (2d8cc65). Not pushed.
